quick.topic: Reuse it or make a new one
quick.summary: How to decide between an existing component and a new one, with three questions.
quick.takeaway: Use it, vary it, or propose it. In that order.

parts.title: Reuse it or make a new one

beats.line: I needed a card with a badge, so I drew one. The system team refused. Why?

board.text: Reuse it or make a new one

beats.line: Because the system already has a card. Ask three questions first.
One. Does an existing component already do the job?
Two. Could a variant of it? A card plus a badge option.
Three. If not, will other teams need the new one too?
Making my own is faster, though.
Faster today. Then two cards drift apart, and both need upkeep.
The card exists. I will propose a badge variant, with my use case.
That one the system team can say yes to.

quiz.question: You need a card that is like the existing one, plus a badge. What should you do first?
options: Check whether a variant of the existing card can do it
Design a new card from scratch
Copy the card and edit it locally
quiz.explanation: A variant keeps one component to maintain and stays consistent across the product.

quiz.question: Creating a new component is always quicker in the long run than extending an existing one.
quiz.explanation: Duplicate components drift apart and both need upkeep; a variant keeps one source.
